title: Road Hazard Protection Purchase Terms and Certificate Price
content:
## 1. Conditions of sale

1.1 Road Hazard Protection is sold only on tires bought from Crestline.

1.2 The covered tire set must be in status ordered or active when the certificate is sold, as the tire set record shows.

1.3 The certificate must be sold no later than the end of the purchase window counted from the purchase of the covered tire set. The window is the plan's purchase window in calendar days, read from the covered set's recorded purchase date; calendar days are counted from the day after the purchase date, so the purchase date plus the number of days is the last qualifying date, and a sale on that last date still qualifies. A window of 0 means the certificate can only be sold on the same ticket as the tires.

1.4 The vehicle's class must be in the plan's list of eligible vehicle classes, and the plan's usage class must match the vehicle: the Commercial LT plan is sold only for a vehicle in commercial use (a vehicle whose usage class is commercial, or a vehicle on a Crestline fleet account roster), and every other plan only for a vehicle in personal use.

## 2. Price

2.1 The price per tire is the plan's percentage of the covered set's unit price, rounded half up to the cent, then raised to the plan's minimum price per tire or lowered to its maximum price per tire when it falls outside them.

2.2 The certificate price is the price per tire multiplied by the number of tires covered.

2.3 The certificate is a line on a store ticket, usually the tire ticket itself. When that ticket is paid with the Crestline card or charged to a fleet account, the ticket total including the certificate posts once, as one card purchase or one fleet invoice.

## Purchase-window boundary (hypothetical dates)

| Plan's window | Set purchased | Last qualifying sale date | Sale on that date | Sale the day after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30 days | March 1 | March 31 | qualifies | does not qualify |
| 30 days | June 10 | July 10 | qualifies | does not qualify |
| 0 days | any date | the tire ticket itself | qualifies on that ticket | does not qualify |

## Price illustration (hypothetical)
A plan of 15 percent, a 14.99 minimum and a 39.99 maximum on a hypothetical unit price of 99.95: 15 percent is 14.9925, rounded to 14.99, which is not below the minimum, so the price per tire is 14.99; on four tires the certificate price is 59.96.
